Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit validation noise; the winning score becomes optimistic ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Nested evaluation or an untouched confirmation holdout addresses selection bias; reusable-holdout methods control adaptive information disclosure ([Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)). These require evaluation arrangements beyond unrestricted repeated score access. Within the pinned protocol, practical mitigation: predeclare search limits, checkpoint evaluation frequency, stopping rules and tie-breaking; record every attempted configuration. These measures reduce opportunities for overfitting but do not establish unbiased post-selection confidence intervals.

For paired uncertainty, retain each model’s binary HR@10 outcome on identical users and candidates. Define d_du = hit_B − hit_A; the macro difference is Δ = ¼Σ_d mean_u(d_du). Resample 200 user pairs with replacement independently within each dataset, preserving model pairing, then recompute Δ for a percentile bootstrap interval ([paired-bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). Report category differences alongside the macro result. One additional net hit changes macro HR@10 by 0.00125. Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty for fixed models, training seed, candidate sets and four datasets; they exclude training-seed and negative-resampling variability and remain exploratory after adaptive selection.

Under the GPU budget, successive halving/Hyperband allocates short runs broadly and longer runs to survivors ([Hyperband](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v18/16-558.html)); it saves compute, not statistical validity. Use a predetermined checkpoint policy and reserve budget for finalists. Interpret results strictly as sampled-candidate HR@10: sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog model comparisons ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Keep the host metric unchanged.
